methodology: Failure scenarios validated under real operating conditions + load test data at 300 concurrent users

scenarios.behavior: Event bus and queue fall back to in-memory mode. Services continue operating.
scenarios.impact: Loss of event persistence and queue durability. No data loss for in-flight requests.
scenarios.recovery: Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff (3 retries, 200ms-2s). Full recovery within 2 seconds of Redis restart.
scenarios.loadImpact: Minimal — in-memory fallback has negligible latency overhead.

scenarios.behavior: Auth service fails on register/login (500 error). Planner and AI continue (no DB dependency).
scenarios.impact: Authentication unavailable. Existing sessions work until token expiry.
scenarios.recovery: Manual restart of auth service required. Prisma auto-reconnect on next query.
scenarios.loadImpact: Auth routes return 500. Non-auth routes unaffected.

scenarios.behavior: Jobs remain in Redis List. New worker picks up where it left off.
scenarios.impact: Delay in job processing equal to worker restart time + poll interval.
scenarios.recovery: Auto-restart of worker within poll interval (500ms-5s). No job loss.
scenarios.loadImpact: Queue backlog grows by ~2-10 jobs per second of downtime.

scenarios.scenario: Auth flood (brute force) during peak traffic
scenarios.behavior: Rate limiter (10 req/min/IP) + brute-force protector (10 req/min/IP) blocks excess.
scenarios.impact: Legitimate users may be rate-limited if sharing an IP.
scenarios.loadImpact: 15/15 flood requests blocked — 100% effective at preventing brute force.

scenarios.behavior: Express JSON parser returns 400 for invalid JSON. Payload size limit (100kb) rejects large payloads with 413.
scenarios.impact: No crash. No database corruption. Input sanitization prevents injection.
scenarios.recovery: Immediate — next valid request processes normally.
scenarios.loadImpact: None — invalid requests rejected at gateway layer.

recoveryTimes.rpo: Plans in memory — lost on restart
Budget tracking in memory — reset on restart

matrix.scenarioSummary: All 5 failure scenarios validated under operating conditions. System degrades gracefully — no cascading failures.

maximumAcceptableDowntime.plannerUnavailable: Low impact (cached plans retained in memory)
maximumAcceptableDowntime.redisUnavailable: Medium impact (queue/event loss risk, in-memory fallback active)

conclusion: System demonstrates graceful degradation and automatic recovery for infrastructure components. Service-level recovery requires manual intervention (no K8s/auto-healing).
recommendations: Add auto-restart for all services (Docker restart policy or PM2 cluster mode)
Implement circuit breaker for downstream service calls
Switch Planner/AI services to Redis-backed state for RPO=0
